ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Three unit circles, each with radius 1 meter, lie in the same plane such that the center of each circle is one intersection point between the two other circles, as shown below. Mass is uniformly distributed among all area enclosed by at least one circle. The mass of the region enclosed by the triangle shown above is $1 \mathrm{~kg}$. Let $x$ be the moment of inertia of the area enclosed by all three circles (intersection, not union) about the axis perpendicular to the page and through the center of mass of the triangle. Then, $x$ can be expressed as $\frac{a \pi-b \sqrt{c}}{d \sqrt{e}}$ $\mathrm{kg} \mathrm{m}^{2}$, where $a, b, c, d, e$ are integers such that $\operatorname{gcd}(a, b, d)=1$ and both $c$ and $e$ are squarefree. Compute $a+b+c+d+e$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three circles of the same size: the red circle is above, the blue circle is at the lower left, and the green circle is at the lower right. The three vertices of the black triangle are located at the pairwise intersection points of the three circles, and also correspond to the circle-center positions of the three circles; the triangle appears to be an equilateral triangle. The central region where the three circles overlap together is enclosed by three 60-degree circular arcs and is in the shape of a Reuleaux triangle. Reasoning: The radii of the three circles are all 1, and the three circle centers form an equilateral triangle with side length 1. The problem gives that the mass of the black equilateral-triangle region is 1 kg, and its area is sqrt(3)/4, so the surface density sigma = 1/(sqrt(3)/4) = 4/sqrt(3). What is required is the polar moment of inertia of the common intersection region of the three circles about the centroid of the equilateral triangle. According to the method draft, decompose the Reuleaux triangle into three sectors with radius 1 and central angle pi/3, and subtract two equilateral triangles. For one sector, the area A_s = (1^2)(pi/3)/2 = pi/6. Its polar second moment about its own circle center is ∫r^2 dA = (pi/3)/4 = pi/12. The distance from the centroid of the equilateral triangle to any vertex is 1/sqrt(3). The centroid of the sector is on the angle bisector, at a distance from the sector's circle center of 4 sin(pi/6)/(3(pi/3)) = 2/pi, so the magnitude of the first moment of one sector is A_s(2/pi)=1/3, in the direction from the vertex toward the triangle centroid. If V is the vector from the triangle centroid to this sector's circle center, then ∫|V+u|^2 dA = |V|^2 A_s + 2V·∫u dA + ∫|u|^2 dA = (1/3)(pi/6) - 2/(3sqrt(3)) + pi/12 = 5pi/36 - 2/(3sqrt(3)). The total for the three sectors is 3(5pi/36 - 2/(3sqrt(3))) = 5pi/12 - 2/sqrt(3). The polar second moment of an equilateral triangle with side length 1 about its centroid is sqrt(3)/48, so the area second moment of the common intersection region is J = 5pi/12 - 2/sqrt(3) - 2(sqrt(3)/48) = 5pi/12 - 17sqrt(3)/24. Multiplying by the surface density gives the mass moment of inertia x = (4/sqrt(3))(5pi/12 - 17sqrt(3)/24) = 5pi/(3sqrt(3)) - 17/6 = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/(6sqrt(3)). Therefore a=10, b=17, c=3, d=6, e=3, and the sum is 10+17+3+6+3=39.

method.method_draft: First read the figure as three congruent unit circles whose centers are the three black triangle vertices; the triangle is equilateral and each side is one radius, so its side length is 1. The desired triple-overlap region is the Reuleaux-triangle-shaped region bounded by three 60-degree circular arcs. From the text, use that the triangle’s mass is 1 kg and mass density is uniform over area, so the surface density is sigma = 1/(sqrt(3)/4) = 4/sqrt(3). Compute the polar second moment of area of the triple-overlap about the triangle centroid by decomposing the Reuleaux triangle as: three radius-1 circular sectors of angle pi/3, minus two copies of the equilateral triangle. For each sector, use local coordinates centered at the sector’s circle center and shift to the common centroid with the parallel-axis expansion integral |V+u|^2 = |V|^2 + 2V·u + |u|^2. Subtract twice the equilateral triangle centroidal polar moment. Multiply the resulting area moment by sigma, put it in the required form (a pi - b sqrt(c))/(d sqrt(e)), then sum a+b+c+d+e.

图像描述：图中有三个同样大小的圆：红圆在上方，蓝圆在左下，绿圆在右下。黑色三角形的三个顶点位于三个圆的两两交点处，并且也对应三个圆的圆心位置；三角形看起来为等边三角形。三个圆共同重叠的中心区域由三段 60 度圆弧围成，是 Reuleaux 三角形形状。
推理：三个圆半径均为 1，三个圆心构成边长为 1 的等边三角形。题给黑色等边三角形区域质量为 1 kg，其面积为 sqrt(3)/4，所以面密度 sigma = 1/(sqrt(3)/4) = 4/sqrt(3)。
要求的是三个圆公共交集区域关于等边三角形质心的极转动惯量。按方法稿，把 Reuleaux 三角形分解为三个半径 1、圆心角 pi/3 的扇形，减去两个等边三角形。
对一个扇形，面积 A_s = (1^2)(pi/3)/2 = pi/6。其关于自身圆心的极二次矩为 ∫r^2 dA = (pi/3)/4 = pi/12。等边三角形质心到任一顶点的距离为 1/sqrt(3)。扇形的质心在角平分线上，距扇形圆心为 4 sin(pi/6)/(3(pi/3)) = 2/pi，因此一扇形的一阶矩大小为 A_s(2/pi)=1/3，方向从顶点指向三角形质心。若 V 为从三角形质心到该扇形圆心的向量，则 ∫|V+u|^2 dA = |V|^2 A_s + 2V·∫u dA + ∫|u|^2 dA = (1/3)(pi/6) - 2/(3sqrt(3)) + pi/12 = 5pi/36 - 2/(3sqrt(3))。
三个扇形合计为 3(5pi/36 - 2/(3sqrt(3))) = 5pi/12 - 2/sqrt(3)。边长 1 的等边三角形关于质心的极二次矩为 sqrt(3)/48，所以公共交集区域面积二次矩为 J = 5pi/12 - 2/sqrt(3) - 2(sqrt(3)/48) = 5pi/12 - 17sqrt(3)/24。
乘以面密度得到质量转动惯量 x = (4/sqrt(3))(5pi/12 - 17sqrt(3)/24) = 5pi/(3sqrt(3)) - 17/6 = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/(6sqrt(3))。因此 a=10, b=17, c=3, d=6, e=3，和为 10+17+3+6+3=39。

所以 J=(3/4)(5pi/9 - 17sqrt(3)/18)=5pi/12 - 17sqrt(3)/24。所求质量转动惯量 x=sigma J=(4/sqrt(3))(5pi/12 - 17sqrt(3)/24)=5pi/(3sqrt(3))-17/6=(10pi-17sqrt(3))/(6sqrt(3)) kg m^2。

于是 a=10, b=17, c=3, d=6, e=3，故 a+b+c+d+e=10+17+3+6+3=39。

raw_record.original_question: Three unit circles, each with radius 1 meter, lie in the same plane such that the center of each circle is one intersection point between the two other circles, as shown below. Mass is uniformly distributed among all area enclosed by at least one circle. The mass of the region enclosed by the triangle shown above is $1 \mathrm{~kg}$. Let $x$ be the moment of inertia of the area enclosed by all three circles (intersection, not union) about the axis perpendicular to the page and through the center of mass of the triangle. Then, $x$ can be expressed as $\frac{a \pi-b \sqrt{c}}{d \sqrt{e}}$ $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$, where $a, b, c, d, e$ are integers such that $\gcd(a, b, d)=1$ and both $c$ and $e$ are squarefree. Compute $a+b+c+d+e$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there are three circles of the same size: the red circle is above, the blue circle is at the lower left, and the green circle is at the lower right. The three vertices of the black triangle are located at the pairwise intersection points of the three circles, and also correspond to the circle-center positions of the three circles; the triangle appears to be an equilateral triangle. The central region where the three circles overlap together is enclosed by three 60-degree circular arcs and is in the shape of a Reuleaux triangle.
Reasoning: The radii of the three circles are all 1, and the three circle centers form an equilateral triangle with side length 1. The problem gives that the mass of the black equilateral-triangle region is 1 kg, and its area is sqrt(3)/4, so the surface density sigma = 1/(sqrt(3)/4) = 4/sqrt(3).
What is required is the polar moment of inertia of the common intersection region of the three circles about the centroid of the equilateral triangle. According to the method draft, decompose the Reuleaux triangle into three sectors with radius 1 and central angle pi/3, and subtract two equilateral triangles.
For one sector, the area A_s = (1^2)(pi/3)/2 = pi/6. Its polar second moment about its own circle center is ∫r^2 dA = (pi/3)/4 = pi/12. The distance from the centroid of the equilateral triangle to any vertex is 1/sqrt(3). The centroid of the sector is on the angle bisector, at a distance from the sector's circle center of 4 sin(pi/6)/(3(pi/3)) = 2/pi, so the magnitude of the first moment of one sector is A_s(2/pi)=1/3, in the direction from the vertex toward the triangle centroid. If V is the vector from the triangle centroid to this sector's circle center, then ∫|V+u|^2 dA = |V|^2 A_s + 2V·∫u dA + ∫|u|^2 dA = (1/3)(pi/6) - 2/(3sqrt(3)) + pi/12 = 5pi/36 - 2/(3sqrt(3)).
The total for the three sectors is 3(5pi/36 - 2/(3sqrt(3))) = 5pi/12 - 2/sqrt(3). The polar second moment of an equilateral triangle with side length 1 about its centroid is sqrt(3)/48, so the area second moment of the common intersection region is J = 5pi/12 - 2/sqrt(3) - 2(sqrt(3)/48) = 5pi/12 - 17sqrt(3)/24.
Multiplying by the surface density gives the mass moment of inertia x = (4/sqrt(3))(5pi/12 - 17sqrt(3)/24) = 5pi/(3sqrt(3)) - 17/6 = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/(6sqrt(3)). Therefore a=10, b=17, c=3, d=6, e=3, and the sum is 10+17+3+6+3=39.
